technologies.name: Blender 4.2 LTS + Cycles (CPU)
technologies.role: production renderer: geometry, shaders, Cycles, export
technologies.gpu: optional; CPU Cycles is a supported backend
technologies.ram: ~2 GB for a 1.3 M-triangle character at 1024²
technologies.cpuFallback: tested here: Cycles CPU rendered the 1.29 M-triangle LÉLU build in 6.02 s at 512²/16 samples
technologies.quality: physically based path tracing with subsurface scattering; the renders in artifacts/foundry/benchmark are Cycles CPU
failures: CPU render time scales with samples; a 1024²/64-sample close-up is tens of seconds, not one
Blender's own GPL does not extend to images it renders or models it exports
technologies.integration: scripts/blender/lelu_foundry_render.py, launched as a child process with a timeout
reasons: free, local, no account, no runtime network
GPL applies to the application we run, not to rendered output
CPU path measured on this machine

technologies.name: PCI-FR 2.3.1 (this repository)
technologies.role: reference-driven component/human reconstruction and persistent identity
inherited: the 39 photographs are the user's own references, read-only
technologies.ram: ~1.5 GB during a build (measured: 58.7 s full character build)
technologies.quality: measured: 1 289 906 triangles, jaw 98.7 mm against the sheet's 96 mm, 149 baby strands with 100 % hairline coverage; the forehead defect is documented, not hidden
failures: component-based, so it cannot invent anatomy the references do not show
the main hair curtain still starts above the rooted fringe (report 2.3.1 §1)
technologies.integration: npm run m23:youth → GLB → the Foundry project store → Cycles
reasons: the only engine here that preserves HER measured identity
zero spend, zero account, zero network
its own diagnostics are the validation input

technologies.name: TripoSR
technologies.role: optional generic single-image prop reconstruction (never the canonical human engine)
inherited: trained on Objaverse renders; the released weights are MIT
technologies.gpu: CUDA recommended; a CPU worker exists in services/asre-reconstruct
technologies.cpuFallback: documented CPU worker in this repository; not timed in this pass
technologies.quality: coarse single-image geometry; fine for props, not a face
failures: single view invents the back of the head
no rig, no eyelids, no hair
technologies.integration: existing ASRE engine "triposr" behind the same job ledger
reasons: MIT code and weights make it legally safe
the mission forbids it as the canonical human reconstruction engine

technologies.name: HumanNOVA
technologies.codeLicense: none — the repository has no LICENSE file (GitHub API: license null)
technologies.weightsLicense: unstated; distributed as an external asset archive
inherited: tokenizer/HMR components borrowed from other projects; unlicensed as redistributed
technologies.gpu: CUDA 12.1 setup script; run.py falls back to CPU only in code
technologies.cpuFallback: the CLI accepts cpu, but the pipeline uses CUDA-only kernels in practice; untested
technologies.quality: CVPR 2026 highlight; paper reports sub-second feed-forward avatars
failures: no licence = no grant to use, modify or redistribute
checkpoint delivered as an external link with no separate terms
reasons: requirement 6/7: a repository without a LICENSE file grants no rights, and 'open source' cannot be assumed
no GPU on this machine; the setup targets CUDA 12.1

technologies.name: IDOL
technologies.weightsLicense: IDOL checkpoint on Hugging Face; SMPL-X/FLAME templates are downloaded separately
inherited: SMPL-X: academic research only (commercial via Meshcapade)
HuGe100K dataset: DeepFashion images may not be redistributed or commercially exploited
technologies.quality: 1K Gaussian avatars, editable; research demonstrations only
failures: registration on the SMPL-X and FLAME sites is mandatory
the SMPL-X licence forbids commercial use and redistribution
24 GB VRAM unavailable here
reasons: account requirement violates Part I (no mandatory accounts)
SMPL-X/FLAME make every output non-commercial
no GPU

technologies.name: PSHuman
technologies.weightsLicense: CC BY 4.0 (reported), with an SMPL-free variant
inherited: SMPL-X templates for the conditioned variant
technologies.quality: detailed clothed humans; users report weak proportions and memory failures
failures: does not fit a 24 GB card, let alone this CPU-only machine
multiview diffusion invents views rather than measuring them
reasons: hardware requirement is an order of magnitude beyond this machine
the mission explicitly forbids making it a default dependency

technologies.name: SAM 3D Body
technologies.role: promptable full-body mesh from one image
technologies.weightsLicense: SAM License (custom Meta terms, not OSI-approved)
technologies.gpu: CUDA unconditionally: the estimator moves its batch to the GPU without checking
technologies.cpuFallback: none — a CPU-only machine raises rather than falling back (independent report)
technologies.quality: strong pose and shape; body only, no identity-level face
failures: Hugging Face access must be requested and approved
no CPU path
custom weight licence needs review before commercial use
reasons: gated checkpoint violates the no-account preference and cannot be fetched offline
no GPU path here

technologies.name: Sapiens2
technologies.role: human vision foundation: pose, segmentation, normals, point maps, matting
inherited: 1B pretrained on human images; training-data terms not restated per checkpoint
technologies.quality: excellent 2D/2.5D human analysis; it is NOT a character generator
failures: cannot produce an editable character mesh
custom licence needs legal review
compute far beyond this machine
technologies.integration: none; could later feed landmarks into PCI-FR
reasons: not a standalone generator (the mission says so and the docs agree)
custom licence + compute

technologies.name: COLMAP
technologies.role: SfM/MVS: camera calibration and dense multi-view geometry
inherited: third-party deps (Ceres, PoseLib, SIFT GPU) separately licensed
technologies.gpu: optional; CPU SfM/MVS supported (CUDA speeds up dense stereo)
technologies.ram: several GB for a dense reconstruction
technologies.quality: the reference implementation for multi-view geometry
failures: needs many calibrated views of ONE static subject; the 39 references are different hairstyles and expressions, not a capture set
technologies.integration: optional CLI behind the Foundry's acquisition step
reasons: legally clean and CPU-capable
no suitable capture set exists, so nothing was claimed

technologies.name: Meshroom / AliceVision
technologies.gpu: the full MVS depth-map step requires an NVIDIA CUDA GPU
technologies.cpuFallback: partial; the MVS stage is CUDA-bound
technologies.quality: good textured meshes from capture sets
failures: CUDA requirement
photogrammetry cannot recover hair or eyelids from these references
reasons: CUDA-bound MVS on a machine with no GPU
wrong tool for a single-subject stylised character

technologies.name: Nerfstudio
technologies.quality: photoreal appearance, not an editable mesh
failures: an appearance representation is not riggable geometry (the mission warns about exactly this)
no GPU
reasons: CUDA-only training
cannot yield the editable, riggable character the Foundry needs

technologies.name: OpenMVS
inherited: AGPL propagates to the combined work if linked into a service
failures: AGPL-3.0 distribution obligations for a hosted product
same capture-set problem as COLMAP
reasons: AGPL-3.0 is incompatible with shipping it inside LÉLU without opening the combined work

technologies.name: SuGaR
technologies.codeLicense: Inria/MPII Gaussian-Splatting licence — research and evaluation only
failures: licence grants non-commercial research use only
needs a splat capture and a GPU
reasons: research-only licence
no GPU, no capture

technologies.name: Stable Fast 3D
technologies.weightsLicense: Stability AI Community License (gated on Hugging Face)
inherited: trained on Objaverse and internal data
failures: gated weights need a Hugging Face account
community licence has revenue and use restrictions
reasons: gated account + restricted licence + no GPU
TripoSR already covers props under MIT
